import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class C2 {
    private Scanner in;
    private PrintWriter out;
    private static final String INPUT = "";
    private static final boolean oj = System.getProperty("ONLINE_JUDGE") != null;

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        new C2().run();
    }

    private void solve() {
        int n = ni();
        int m = ni();
        
        // The maximum number of spider-free cells is achieved when we minimize
        // the number of occupied cells after one second.
        // Each spider can move to one of 5 positions (including staying).
        // We want to maximize cells with 0 spiders.
        // This is equivalent to minimizing the number of cells that have at least one spider.
        // 
        // Key insight: We can model this as a matching problem where each spider
        // chooses a destination cell. We want to maximize cells with no spiders.
        // 
        // For an n x m grid, the optimal strategy is to group spiders into groups
        // that can all move to the same cell. The minimum number of occupied cells
        // is ceil(n*m / 5) because each cell can receive up to 5 spiders (from itself
        // and 4 neighbors).
        //
        // Therefore, maximum spider-free cells = n*m - ceil(n*m / 5)
        // = n*m - (n*m + 4) / 5
        
        int total = n * m;
        int minOccupied = (total + 4) / 5; // This is ceil(total / 5)
        out.println(total - minOccupied);
    }

    private void run() throws Exception {
        in = new Scanner(System.in);
        out = new PrintWriter(System.out);
        solve();
        out.flush();
    }

    private int ni() { return Integer.parseInt(in.next()); }
    private long nl() { return Long.parseLong(in.next()); }
    private double nd() { return Double.parseDouble(in.next()); }
}
